artworks.title: Hippolytus Saved from Death (Virbius)
artworks.description: Tempesta's Metamorphoses plate — Aesculapius restoring Hippolytus at Diana's bidding, the youth renamed Virbius as Ovid's Book XV inset ends.

artworks.title: Hippolytus Saved and Named Virbius
artworks.description: Vieira Lusitano's Ovid scene — Diana's impulse, Aesculapius' revival, and the new name Virbius in the sacred grove.

artworks.title: The Death of Hippolytus (La mort d'Hippolyte)
artworks.description: Lemoyne's Louvre marble — Poseidon's sea-bull wrecks the chariot, the death Ovid's inset must reverse before Virbius rises.

artworks.title: The Death of Hippolytus
artworks.description: Alma-Tadema's shore — the bull from the waves and the wrecked hunter, Phaedra's lie completed before Diana's rescue.

popCulture.title: Hippolytus (play)
popCulture.creator: Euripides
popCulture.description: Euripides' tragedy of the chaste hunter and the stepmother's desire — the Greek source Ovid retells before Virbius' grove.

popCulture.title: Phèdre
popCulture.creator: Jean Racine
popCulture.description: Racine's French classic remakes Hippolytus' doom for the neoclassical stage — passion as fatal clarity, still the inset's afterlife.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Book XV's Virbius inset — Poseidon's bull, the wrecked chariot, and Diana hiding the restored youth in her sacred grove.
